definitions.explanation: A streak of light in the sky caused by a small particle from space burning up as it enters Earth's atmosphere.

examples.japanese: ⟦{昨夜|さくや}→昨夜：02999_sakuya⟧、{流星|りゅうせい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}た→見る：00283_miru⟧。
examples.english: I saw a shooting star last night.

examples.japanese: {流星|りゅうせい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{願|ねが}いごと→願い事：14621_negaigoto⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I made a wish on a shooting star.

examples.japanese: ⟦{今夜|こんや}→今夜：01411_konya⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{流星群|りゅうせいぐん}→流星群：20408_ryuuseigun⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}られる→見る：00283_miru⟧⟦らしい→らしい：09502_rashii⟧。
examples.english: Apparently, we can see a meteor shower tonight.

notes:
{流星|りゅうせい} refers to what is commonly called a "shooting star" in English.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- ⟦{流星群|りゅうせいぐん}→流星群：20408_ryuuseigun⟧ (meteor shower)
- {流星|りゅうせい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}る→見る：00283_miru⟧ (see a shooting star)
- {流星|りゅうせい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{願|ねが}う→願う：02387_negau⟧ (wish upon a shooting star)

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{流|なが}れ{星|ぼし}→流れ星：05049_nagareboshi⟧: colloquial term for shooting star
- ⟦{隕石|いんせき}→隕石：05054_inseki⟧: meteorite (one that reaches the ground)
- ⟦{彗星|すいせい}→彗星：05053_suisei⟧: comet

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, as in many cultures, there is a tradition of making wishes when seeing a shooting star. The belief is that if you can make a wish before the star disappears, it will come true.
